review_reference: Owner decisions in chat by D-Eminence (unsigned until the owner signs). Q24, 2026-11-04: "yes" - build patient chat PART 2 now: (a) lab results in the PATIENT chat only from finished visits (results from cancelled, wrong-patient or still-open visits must not reach the patient chat; the staff chat keeps full access); (b) the server side of the "Discussed with the patient" mark for sensitive and critical results (Ola builds the EHR button): a clinician with care access to the patient marks a released result as discussed; once marked, that sensitive result may appear in the patient chat with the server-added talk-to-your-doctor line; unmarking (withdrawal) allowed with a reason; every mark audited; (c) migration 0121 (0106-0120 are applied before it in the release, but it relies on none of their objects). Q28: "keep" - the PR 1 safer defaults stay (sensitive diagnoses and their medicines stay out; Ola still approves the talk-to-your-doctor wording and the final sensitive test list). Design decisions the owner confirms by signing (two need the owner or Ola, each a one-line change if overridden: D-B and D-C): D-A permission lab.result.discuss for roles doctor and clinician (not nurse); the list uses lab.result.released.read. D-B a result is gated when its last released version is sensitive (PR 1's unchanged list, kept in the services' code) or critical (abnormal_flag critical_candidate): critical results are newly held back from the patient chat until discussed. D-C marking and withdrawing need an active direct-care write_records grant (never break-glass); listing needs read_records. D-D a withdrawal names a reason code (marked_in_error, not_yet_discussed, wrong_patient, other) and a reason of 8-500 characters, stored only in lab.result_discussion_events, never in audit.events, a log or a response. D-E a mark binds one result version; a released correction needs a new mark; withdrawing needs no currency check. D-F a finished visit is: encounter completed, lab request active, on hold or completed, route (if any) seen and not ended wrong_patient or entered_in_error (a route the gate cannot see reads as not finished). D-G the sensitive list stays in TypeScript; the database stores only marks. D-H two trails: the append-only event table and lab-api's ids-only audit.events row per call.
evidence: 0121 Lab result discussions (patient chat part 2), written on f11c9ec9 (migrations through 0105). ORDER: 0121, then lab-api, then ehr-api. 0106-0120 are not required: 0121 uses and requires none of their objects and applies on 0105 alone; its preconditions pin the bodies it relies on as 0001-0105 left them, so if one of 0106-0120 replaces one of those bodies (lab.patient_self_context, ehr.patient_self_context, identity.has_active_consent_grant, auth.membership_has_permission, the five platform.current_* readers, platform.reject_mutation), 0121 refuses with 55000 and nothing is applied; the bodies are then measured again. The 0105 marker is only the existence of ehr.resolve_document_scan_target (0121 neither calls nor reads it, so 0106-0120 may rewrite its body). On this branch alone the release contract refuses the empty 0106-0120 slots (verify-release-contract and release/test/staging-migration-ledger.test.mjs: missing migration prefix, expected); components.json says 107 files, last 0121, and verify-migration-ledger passes 107 immutable migrations. Rollout and failure behaviour: ehr-api first is fine (old lab-api never sends a gated row; critical rows without _discussed are now dropped, the safe direction); lab-api before 0121 makes its patient query fail, so the patient chat treats Lab as unavailable (Lab results drop out, history citing a lab result answers 503); the release runs migrations first. Old services on 0121: today's lab-api and ehr-api never call the new functions and their queries read as before (the new work-item policy applies to the owner only). WHAT IT DOES: (S1) lab.result_discussion_events, append-only (platform.reject_mutation on UPDATE and DELETE), FORCE row-level security with one SELECT and one INSERT policy (true), no privilege for any role, strictly alternating marks and withdrawals per released result version (odd event_no discussed, even withdrawn; the reason check is null-safe), keyed to lab.result_releases (result_id, result_version) and to the actor's membership, idempotency unique per facility, account and key. (S2) policy lab_work_items_patient_result_gate on lab.work_items, SELECT, TO the owner only, USING lab.patient_self_context(patient_id): under an owner that does not bypass row-level security the patient gate can otherwise not reach the visit; no runtime role is the owner or a member of it (precondition and suite), and the Lab runtime still reads no work item in a patient session. (S3) lab.result_visit_finished(uuid,uuid,uuid) and lab.result_discussion_target(uuid,uuid) (owner only); lab.patient_self_result_gates(uuid) returns (result_id, released_version, finished_visit, discussed) in that patient's own patient-self session only; lab.record_result_discussion(uuid,uuid,bigint,text,text) and lab.withdraw_result_discussion(uuid,uuid,bigint,text,text,text,text) return (event_id, event_no, state, occurred_at, finished_visit, replayed); lab.list_result_discussions(uuid) returns (result_id, result_version, test_code_system, test_code, test_name, abnormal_flag, released_at, finished_visit, discussion_state, discussion_event_no, discussion_at, discussion_by_membership_id, withdrawal_reason_code), never the reason text. All SECURITY DEFINER but the target helper, search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp, owned by lab.results' owner, plpgsql ones in the RDS form (#variable_conflict use_column); EXECUTE on the four commands for hid_lab_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime only, never PUBLIC. Refusals: 42501 LAB_CONTEXT_REQUIRED, PURPOSE_OF_USE_REQUIRED, PERMISSION_DENIED, PATIENT_ACCESS_DENIED; 22023 RESULT_DISCUSSION_INVALID; P0002 RESULT_NOT_FOUND; P0001 RESULT_VERSION_CHANGED, RESULT_NOT_RELEASED, RESULT_ENTERED_IN_ERROR, RESULT_NOT_DISCUSSED, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED, RESULT_DISCUSSION_CHANGED (a repeated request whose event is no longer the version's state: a replayed withdrawal after a new mark, or a replayed mark after a withdrawal, is refused instead of misreporting what the patient sees). The record command's local path checks the version against the last released one (what the list and the patient gate offer), not lab.results.current_version, so a pending unreleased correction does not block marking the released version (an older released version answers RESULT_VERSION_CHANGED, a newer one RESULT_NOT_RELEASED). Serialized per (result, version) by a transaction advisory lock (not FOR UPDATE, 0105 S4); the Idempotency-Key is looked up again after the lock (a duplicate in flight replays), and the same key raced for another (result, version) meets the key's unique index and answers IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. lab.list_result_discussions returns every released result, newest first (no cut before lab-api's sensitive and critical gate); lab-api keeps at most 500 gated rows and reports truncated. (S4) permission lab.result.discuss, role rows doctor and clinician (0084's ON CONFLICT form). No audit row, account or role row is written by the migration; the commands write no audit row (lab-api does). runtime-grants.sql gains a 0121 block after 0105's (EXECUTE on the four commands for hid_lab_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime; revoke from PUBLIC on the six functions and the event table). Preconditions (catalog reads only; 55000 or 42501, nothing applied): 0105's ehr.resolve_document_scan_target present as the marker (its body is not pinned); not applied yet ('0121: already applied'); the ten pinned bodies (lab.patient_self_context 39aeca12, ehr.patient_self_context 9878cfbd, identity.has_active_consent_grant 732d1189, auth.membership_has_permission 65e3eaff, current_actor_subject cf14c2d4, current_membership_id 64198970, current_facility_id c4a7c298, current_purpose_of_use 74f7f2ea, current_correlation_id 48d3bf18, reject_mutation 398738f3, each measured on a fresh 0105 database); the 58 columns read with their types and NOT NULLs, the unique (result_id, result_version) release key and the membership key; the ten patient-self policies of 0030 and 0067; 0086's order_routes_command_read on ehr.order_routes (SELECT, USING true, for PUBLIC), through which the owner sees a result's route in a patient-self session; FORCE row-level security on lab.work_items; one owner for the eleven tables, an applier that is it or a member that inherits it and may SET ROLE to it, no runtime role a member of it, and that owner's schema, table and EXECUTE privileges never through a superuser's bypass; roles doctor and clinician. Post-checks pin every function's attributes, owner and exact ACL, the table's row-level security, policies, trigger and empty ACL, the owner-only policy's roles and expression, and exactly the two role rows. Locks (pg_locks before commit on a 0105 copy): SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on lab.result_releases, identity.patients, identity.facilities and identity.staff_facility_memberships (the new foreign keys); ROW EXCLUSIVE on auth.permissions and auth.role_permissions; ACCESS SHARE on the tables the SQL bodies read; ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on lab.work_items (CREATE POLICY, last); behind a session holding ACCESS SHARE on lab.work_items the runner stopped after its 5 s lock_timeout (5.3-5.5 s) with nothing applied, and applied once the holder ended. PROOF on throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 (local clusters, deleted after): a FRESH install by the runner on a new cluster with no runtime roles (107 pending, dry run rolled back with no ledger table left, 107 applied, the four commands owner-only until the role bootstrap, then EXECUTE for hid_lab_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime; bootstrap and --verify-only pass; the runner again 0 pending; the file again by hand answers '0121: already applied'; 1218 non-owner grants); an UPGRADE of a 0105 database built by f11c9ec9's runner and bootstrapped with f11c9ec9's runtime-grants.sql (1210 non-owner grants; plan 1 pending; dry run rolled back with 106 ledger rows and no table, gate or permission left; apply in 30-41 ms; then 0 pending, a re-run 0 pending, the file again answers already applied; 1218 non-owner grants after the migration alone, the eight new being the four commands' EXECUTE for the two runtime roles; this branch's bootstrap then changes none and the new ACLs equal the fresh install's; --verify-only passes); all 80 database suites pass on both (78 existing, with order-routes-privileges now pinning the 0121 policy among lab.work_items' policies, and the new lab-result-discussions suite). The new suite (test/database/lab-result-discussions.integration.sql, 119 cases, rollback-only: 118 checked before the non-bypass section's savepoint rollback, which would otherwise discard that section's rows, and the 520-result long list in its own savepoint; every case as hid_lab_runtime with lab-api's exact app.* settings): the gate for finished visits (completed encounter and active, on-hold or completed request true; encounter in progress, cancelled or entered in error, request cancelled or entered in error, a route ended wrong_patient false; an ordinary routed result true), isolation (patient A asking for B, no context and staff context: no row), marks and versions (discussed, withdrawn, discussed again; a released v2 correction not discussed until v2 is marked), the runtime role (no work item in a patient session, no right on the event table or the two helpers), record (ok, replay, key reuse, new key while discussed, wrong purpose, no correlation, nurse, no grant, break-glass only, read grant only, bad arguments, another patient's or facility's result, unreleased, stale, correction pending, invalidated, routed by the ordering facility, routed entered in error, routed wrong patient, the performing lab refused), withdraw (ok as event 2, replay, not discussed, bad code, 7 and 501 characters, outer spaces, unreleased version, nurse, marked again as event 3, the old version after a correction), the table (UPDATE and DELETE refused even for the owner, the alternation, reason and release checks), the list (11 rows, local and routed, state, version, codes, never the reason text, a nurse and a read grant may list, no grant, the patient's session and no correlation refused), the stored rows and no audit row; and with the owner moved inside the transaction to a fresh NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role: the gate, mark, withdraw, routed mark, refusals and list again, then without the owner-only policy the gate loses the row (the policy is needed). Review fixes, each proved on PostgreSQL 16 fresh and as an upgrade from 0105: a replayed withdrawal after a new mark and a replayed mark after a withdrawal answer RESULT_DISCUSSION_CHANGED, a replayed mark while marked again its own event; marking the last released version while a correction is pending succeeds and reaches the patient gate; with ehr.order_routes' read policy narrowed to staff sessions the gate reads a wrong-patient route and an ordinary route as not finished; the list returns 531 rows for a patient with 520 newer results, the oldest included. Two-session races (the suite's fixtures committed in a database copy): the same withdrawal twice in flight answers the second as a replay (event 2, replayed) and the same mark likewise; one key raced for two results answers IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED for the mark and the withdrawal; with the pre-fix bodies the same races answer RESULT_NOT_DISCUSSED and 23505. 0121 applies on a 0105 copy whose ehr.resolve_document_scan_target body was rewritten, and refuses (55000, nothing applied) on one whose order_routes_command_read was narrowed. Mutants of the visit check (no route check, cancelled request accepted), of the gate (a mark on any version counts) and of the record command (a read grant enough) are each killed. services/ehr-api/scripts/test-staging-schema-upgrade.mjs passes with 0121 as the declared migration (HID_BASELINE_RUNTIME_GRANTS = f11c9ec9's runtime-grants.sql): a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator applies the 106-file baseline, the dry run rolls back, 0121 applies, checksums kept, no existing table's row-level security changed, the migration's grants match runtime-grants.sql, clean install too. On a database built 0001-0121 with MIGRATION_TARGET=rds by a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner (applier = owner), the new suite passed all its cases with owner_bypasses_rls false (measured before the review fixes) (the owner-only policy proved needed there too); on that owner the other suites fail exactly as on a 0105 database built the same way (schema, ocr-outbox-insert and sealed-demo-story, which count the hid_-named owner itself), and no other. Also run: verify-migration-ledger (107 immutable migrations, 0121 last); services/ehr-api/scripts/test-platform-administration.mjs passes (26 checks, MIGRATION_TARGET=rds); scripts/tuf-staging-migration-rehearsal.mjs passes its schema stages (existing_schema_upgrade 0028 to 0121 with the dry run unchanged and every seed verified, additional_schema_suites, otp, patient and emergency-contact runtimes) and then stops in this sandbox at the facility self sign-up runtime for an environment reason (services/notification-api has no node_modules), unrelated to 0121.
